newsitem.title: UK: EU flouting free trade on beef - British minister.
newsitem.headline: EU flouting free trade on beef - British minister.

text.p: Britain's agriculture minister on Tuesday accused European Union states of flouting "every principle" of the bloc's free trade policy in maintaining the ban on exports of British beef.
Speaking to the annual conference of the ruling Conservative Party, Douglas Hogg also said there was no point in slaughtering thousands of extra cattle to eradicate "mad cow" disease.

As angry farmers demonstrated outside the conference hall, Hogg made clear he would not succumb to EU demands for a cull of up to 147,000 cows most at risk from Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE).

"By the turn of this century, 2001 or thereabouts, BSE will largely have disappeared from the national herd. There is no credible cull policy which will substantially accelerate the rate of decline or materially bring forward the date when it is totally eradicated," Hogg told delegates.
Britain's refusal to go along with the EU cull has caused prospects for a lifting of the export ban, imposed after scientists found BSE could be transmitted to humans, to recede.
But Hogg said the ban flouted the principle of the single market on which trade among member states is based.
"The European ban goes against every principle of the single market. It has destroyed a flourishing export market. I say to the Europeans...restore consumer confidence, lift the ban."

Hogg announced plans to speed up a cull already taking place under the government's control of cattle more than 30 months old and to increase compensation for British farmers whose markets have been hit by the BSE scare.
